a1102.t:
Le 8 février 2025, lors du sommet EAC-SADC à Dar es Salaam, le président rwandais Paul Kagame a rejeté les accusations de la RDC et imputé l’escalade des tensions à Kinshasa, appelant à des actions concrètes pour résoudre la crise sécuritaire dans l’est de la RDC.
Le sommet conjoint de la Communauté d’Afrique de l’Est (EAC) et de la Communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe (SADC), qui s’est tenu à Dar es Salaam le 8 février 2025, a été marqué par une déclaration percutante du président rwandais, Paul Kagame. Lors des discussions sur la crise sécuritaire dans l’est de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Kagame a directement imputé l’escalade des tensions à Kinshasa.
Kagame a rejeté toute responsabilité du Rwanda dans les accusations formulées par la RDC. Il a dénoncé une stratégie délibérée de Kinshasa, cherchant à impliquer Kigali dans un conflit qu’il considère comme ne relevant pas de son pays.
« Personne ne peut nous dire de la fermer »
Face aux accusations congolaises, Kagame a exprimé son mécontentement, affirmant qu’il était inacceptable que la RDC tente de faire taire le Rwanda alors qu’elle alimentait une crise de sécurité contre lui. « Personne ne peut nous dire de la fermer », a-t-il martelé, soulignant que le Rwanda avait multiplié les appels au dialogue sans réponse de la part des autorités congolaises.
« Nous supplions la RDC et ses dirigeants depuis longtemps. Nous avons partagé nos problèmes et demandé à la RDC de les aborder, et ils ont refusé », a-t-il ajouté.
Une guerre aux racines ethniques selon Kagame
Kagame a insisté sur le fait que la crise actuelle en RDC était profondément ancrée dans des tensions ethniques anciennes, exacerbées par des politiques de marginalisation. Il a averti que cette situation pourrait avoir de graves répercussions à l’échelle régionale et souligné que le Rwanda ne pouvait pas rester passif face à cette évolution.
« Ce qui se passe là-bas, c’est une guerre ethnique qui se prépare depuis longtemps, déniant les droits des gens et attaquant ensuite le Rwanda. Vous devez reconnaître les droits des gens et faire un pas pour résoudre le problème », a-t-il expliqué.
Le président rwandais a également rejeté toute responsabilité dans le conflit, soulignant que la RDC en était le principal instigateur. « Cette guerre a été déclenchée par la RDC et non par le Rwanda. Elle a été imposée sur nous et on nous a demandé de l’assumer. Nous ne pouvons pas l’accepter », a-t-il déclaré.
Des résolutions pour restaurer la stabilité
Malgré ces tensions, le sommet a permis d’adopter plusieurs résolutions visant à restaurer la stabilité dans l’est de la RDC. Les chefs d’État présents ont exigé un cessez-le-feu immédiat, la réouverture de l’aéroport de Goma et la reprise des négociations avec toutes les parties, y compris le groupe rebelle M23.
Une réunion des chefs des forces de défense de l’EAC et de la SADC est prévue dans les cinq jours pour élaborer des stratégies de sécurisation de la région et de facilitation de l’aide humanitaire. Le sommet a également insisté sur la nécessité de neutraliser les FDLR et d’établir un plan de retrait des forces armées étrangères non invitées du territoire congolais.
Kagame appelle à des solutions concrètes
Kagame a averti contre l’inefficacité des rencontres diplomatiques qui ne débouchent pas sur des actions concrètes. Il a exhorté les participants à ne pas se contenter de discussions stériles et à œuvrer activement pour des solutions durables.
« Ne nous contentons pas d’une autre réunion comme celle que nous avons eue. Utilisons cette rencontre de manière à prendre en compte sérieusement toutes ces questions et trouvons une solution durable », a-t-il conclu.
Les tensions entre Kigali et Kinshasa demeurent vives, alimentées par des affrontements armés et des accusations mutuelles de soutien à des groupes rebelles. Bien que des engagements aient été pris lors du sommet, leur mise en œuvre reste incertaine, compte tenu des divergences profondes entre les deux pays.
AC/APA
Source: https://fr.apanews.net/
a1102.en:
On 8 February 2025, at the EAC-SADC summit in Dar es Salaam, Rwandan President Paul Kagame rejected the DRC's accusations and attributed the escalation of tensions to Kinshasa, calling for concrete actions to resolve the security crisis in eastern DRC.
The joint summit of the East African Community (EAC) and the Southern African Development Community (SADC), held in Dar es Salaam on 8 February 2025, was marked by a striking statement from the Rwandan president, Paul Kagame. During the discussions on the security crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Kagame directly attributed the escalation of tensions to Kinshasa.
Kagame rejected any responsibility of Rwanda in the accusations formulated by the DRC. He denounced a deliberate strategy by Kinshasa, seeking to implicate Kigali in a conflict that he considers does not concern his country.
"No one can tell us to shut up"
Faced with the Congolese accusations, Kagame expressed his displeasure, stating that it was unacceptable for the DRC to try to silence Rwanda while it was fuelling a security crisis against it. "No one can tell us to shut up," he hammered, underlining that Rwanda had made repeated calls for dialogue without a response from the Congolese authorities.
"We have been begging the DRC and its leaders for a long time. We have shared our problems and asked the DRC to address them, and they have refused," he added.
A war with ethnic roots according to Kagame
Kagame insisted that the current crisis in the DRC was deeply rooted in old ethnic tensions, exacerbated by policies of marginalisation. He warned that this situation could have serious repercussions at the regional level and underlined that Rwanda could not remain passive in the face of this development.
"What is happening there is an ethnic war that has been in preparation for a long time, denying people's rights and then attacking Rwanda. You must recognise people's rights and take a step to solve the problem," he explained.
The Rwandan president also rejected any responsibility in the conflict, underlining that the DRC was its main instigator. "This war was triggered by the DRC and not by Rwanda. It was imposed on us and we were asked to bear it. We cannot accept it," he declared.
Resolutions to restore stability
Despite these tensions, the summit made it possible to adopt several resolutions aimed at restoring stability in eastern DRC. The heads of State present demanded an immediate ceasefire, the reopening of Goma airport and the resumption of negotiations with all parties, including the M23 rebel group.
A meeting of the chiefs of the EAC and SADC defence forces is planned within five days to develop strategies for securing the region and facilitating humanitarian aid. The summit also insisted on the need to neutralise the FDLR and to establish a plan for the withdrawal of uninvited foreign armed forces from Congolese territory.
Kagame calls for concrete solutions
Kagame warned against the ineffectiveness of diplomatic meetings that do not lead to concrete actions. He urged participants not to settle for sterile discussions and to work actively for lasting solutions.
"Let us not settle for another meeting like the one we have had. Let us use this meeting in a way that seriously takes into account all these questions and let us find a lasting solution," he concluded.
Tensions between Kigali and Kinshasa remain high, fuelled by armed clashes and mutual accusations of support for rebel groups. Although commitments were made at the summit, their implementation remains uncertain, given the deep divergences between the two countries.
AC/APA
Source: https://fr.apanews.net/

a1209.t:
Le Maroc achemine de l’aide médicale à Gaza, alors que le nombre de Palestiniens tués par les forces d’occupation israéliennes alors qu’ils cherchaient de l’aide continue d’augmenter.
Des camions transportant de l’aide médicale et alimentaire marocaine sont arrivés à Gaza, apportant un soulagement indispensable à la population palestinienne qui souffre du blocus israélien et du génocide en cours.
Une vidéo diffusée lundi par l’agence Bayt Mal Al-Quds montre des camions chargés de fournitures sillonnant les rues de Gaza. Les camions arboraient le drapeau marocain et le logo de la Fondation Mohammed V pour la Solidarité.
Des équipes ont accompagné les camions pendant qu’ils livraient l’aide aux entrepôts, où elle était déchargée.
L’agence a ensuite publié des photos montrant l’aide alimentaire marocaine, notamment des aliments pour bébés, des conserves, de la farine et des fruits, atteignant des centres de stockage à Deir el-Balah, une ville du centre de Gaza.
Ce soutien intervient dans un contexte de grande difficulté. Gaza est confrontée à une crise humanitaire de plus en plus grave en raison du blocus israélien, qui a entraîné une malnutrition et une famine généralisées . De nombreux hôpitaux peinent à fonctionner et les produits de première nécessité sont devenus rares et inabordables pour la plupart des habitants.
Le Maroc a envoyé plusieurs lots d’aide à Gaza ces derniers jours. Cette aide a été saluée par de nombreux Palestiniens, qui affirment qu’elle contribue à répondre à des besoins urgents. Cependant, les organisations humanitaires préviennent que le volume de l’aide est encore loin d’être suffisant.
Le service de presse du gouvernement de Gaza a indiqué que seuls 85 camions d’aide humanitaire étaient entrés dans l’enclave hier, et que nombre d’entre eux avaient été pillés avant d’atteindre les personnes dans le besoin. Le service de presse et les Nations Unies ont tous deux indiqué qu’entre 500 et 600 camions étaient nécessaires chaque jour pour apporter une aide adéquate à la population, réduire les pillages et faire baisser les prix élevés causés par les pénuries.
Ce chiffre n’a jamais été atteint depuis que l’aide a été autorisée à entrer à Gaza après un long retard causé par le siège israélien.
La situation demeure extrêmement dangereuse. Selon le ministère de la Santé de Gaza, au moins 135 Palestiniens ont été tués lors d’attaques israéliennes au cours des dernières 24 heures, dont 87 personnes qui attendaient de l’aide. Ces attaques ont également fait 771 blessés.
Le ministère a indiqué que cinq personnes sont mortes de faim au cours de la même période, portant le nombre total de décès liés à la faim à 193, dont 96 enfants.
Trois autres corps ont été retrouvés sous les décombres des bombardements israéliens précédents.
Le nombre de Palestiniens tués en quête d’aide humanitaire a également continué d’augmenter. Depuis le 27 mai, date à laquelle Israël a mis en place un nouveau système controversé de distribution d’aide par l’intermédiaire de la Fondation humanitaire de Gaza (GHF), 1 655 personnes en quête d’aide ont été tuées et plus de 11 800 blessées.
MK/Sf/ac/APA
a1209.en:
Moroccan medical aid arrives in Gaza amid famine crisis

Morocco is delivering medical aid to Gaza, as the number of Palestinians killed by the Israeli occupation forces while seeking aid continues to rise.

Trucks carrying Moroccan medical and food aid have arrived in Gaza, bringing much-needed relief to the Palestinian population suffering from the Israeli blockade and the ongoing genocide.

A video released on Monday by the Bayt Mal Al-Quds agency shows trucks loaded with supplies driving through the streets of Gaza. The trucks bore the Moroccan flag and the logo of the Mohammed V Foundation for Solidarity.

Teams accompanied the trucks as they delivered the aid to warehouses, where it was unloaded.

The agency later published photos showing Moroccan food aid, including baby food, canned goods, flour and fruit, arriving at storage centres in Deir el-Balah, a city in central Gaza.

This support comes in a context of great hardship. Gaza is facing an increasingly severe humanitarian crisis due to the Israeli blockade, which has led to widespread malnutrition and famine. Many hospitals are struggling to function and basic necessities have become scarce and unaffordable for most residents.

Morocco has sent several consignments of aid to Gaza in recent days. This aid has been welcomed by many Palestinians, who say it helps meet urgent needs. However, humanitarian organisations warn that the volume of aid is still far from sufficient.

The Gaza government press service reported that only 85 trucks of humanitarian aid entered the enclave yesterday, and that many of them had been looted before reaching people in need. The press service and the United Nations both stated that between 500 and 600 trucks were needed each day to bring adequate aid to the population, reduce looting and bring down the high prices caused by shortages.

That figure has never been reached since aid was allowed to enter Gaza after a long delay caused by the Israeli siege.

The situation remains extremely dangerous. According to the Gaza Ministry of Health, at least 135 Palestinians were killed in Israeli attacks over the past 24 hours, including 87 people who were waiting for aid. These attacks also left 771 people wounded.

The ministry said that five people died of starvation during the same period, bringing the total number of hunger-related deaths to 193, including 96 children.

Three more bodies were recovered from the rubble of earlier Israeli bombardments.

The number of Palestinians killed while seeking humanitarian aid has also continued to rise. Since 27 May, when Israel put in place a new and controversial aid distribution system through the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), 1,655 people seeking aid have been killed and more than 11,800 wounded.

MK/Sf/ac/APA

a1492.t: የአሜሪካ ፕሬዚዳንት ዶናልድ ትራምፕ በካናዳ እየተካሄደ የነበረውን የቡድን ሰባት አባል አገሮች መሪዎችን ስብሰባ አቋርጠው ወደ አገራቸው ሲመለሱ ለጋዜጠኞች ከተናገሩት የተወሰደ፡፡ ፕሬዚዳንት ትራምፕ የቡድን ሰባት አባል አገሮች የመሪዎች ስብሰባ አቋርጠው መመለሳቸውን በተመለከተ፣ የፈረንሣይ ፕሬዚዳንት ኢማኑኤል ማክሮን ለጋዜጠኞች በሰጡት መግለጫ፣ ‹‹ፕሬዚዳንት ትራምፕ ስብሰባውን አቋርጠው ወደ አሜሪካ የተመለሱት እስራኤልና ኢራን የተኩስ አቁም እንዲያደርጉ ለማግባባት ነው…›› ብለው ነበር፡፡ ነገር ግን ፕሬዚዳንት ትራምፕ የፈረንሣዩን አቻቸውን ንግግር አጣጥለውታል፡፡ ‹‹ፕሬዚዳንት ማክሮን የተመለስኩበትን ምክንያት ባለመረዳት ተሳስተዋል፡፡ እኔ ወደ አሜሪካ የምመለሰው ከተኩስ አቁም በላይ የበለጠ ትልቅ ነገር ስለምንፈልግ ነው…›› ብለዋል፡፡ የሁለቱ አገሮች ግጭት ወደ አደገኛ ምዕራፍ እየገባ ባለበት ጊዜም የተኩስ አቁም አስፈላጊ እንዳልሆነ የገለጹት ትራምፕ፣ ኢራን የኑክሌር ባለቤት መሆን የለባትም በማለት የቴህራን ነዋሪዎችም በፍጥነት መኖሪያቸውን ለቀው እንዲወጡ አስጠንቅቀዋል፡፡
a1492.en:
“We are looking for something much bigger than a ceasefire for the Israel-Iran conflict”

The following is taken from what U.S. President Donald Trump told journalists as he cut short the summit of the leaders of the Group of Seven member countries being held in Canada and returned to his country. Regarding President Trump’s departure from the G7 leaders’ summit before its conclusion, French President Emmanuel Macron said in a statement to journalists: “President Trump cut the meeting short and returned to America in order to persuade Israel and Iran to agree to a ceasefire…” But President Trump dismissed his French counterpart’s remarks. “President Macron is mistaken because he does not understand the reason for my return. I am returning to America because we want something much bigger than a ceasefire…” he said. At a time when the conflict between the two countries is entering a dangerous phase, Trump, who stated that a ceasefire was not necessary, said that Iran must not be allowed to possess nuclear weapons, and warned the residents of Tehran to leave their homes quickly.

a1664.t:
By Dorica Mtenje
LILONGWE, Maravipost: In the midst of hunger, Apostle Clifford Kawinga of Salvation for All Ministries has distributed maize to four districts in the southern region: Neno, Zomba, Chikwawa, and Mwanza.
During the donation event held at Kanyimbiri Primary School in Chikwawa, Kawinga provided maize to 2,500 beneficiaries.
This initiative is part of the ministry’s mission to offer both spiritual nourishment and material support to communities in need.
Kawinga stated that the outreach also marks the official opening of a new branch of the church, further expanding the ministry’s efforts to spread the gospel and serve the community.
“We believe that through our new branch, we will support many souls through spiritual encouragement and humanitarian aid,” said Kawinga.
Receiving the donation, Charles Kanjoka, on behalf of Senior Chief Makuwira, expressed gratitude for Kawinga’s encouragement in their spiritual lives.
Kanjoka noted that the donation is timely, as the area has been severely impacted by several recent cyclones.
He encouraged Kawinga and his team to continue their efforts to reach out to those in need with both spiritual and humanitarian assistance.

a1855.t:
A Nigerian diaspora group, the Zumunta Association USA Inc., said on Monday that it will train 1000 youths in ICT and Artificial Intelligence (AI) during its 2025 Annual Convention.
At a joint news Conference in Abuja on Monday, Its National President, Mr Sunday Bitrus, also disclosed that the convention, which is the association’s second in Nigeria in its 35 years of existence, will hold in Nasarawa State.
He said the 2025 Zumunta Convention will feature a robust lineup of other high-impact programmes, which include a free medical outreach, golf and tennis tournaments.
Others are strategic business meetings on key sectors including agriculture, mining, health, and housing, as well as participation in the National Diaspora Day and Diaspora Week activities in Abuja.
According to Bitrus, the convention, themed “From Connection to Action: Mobilizing Local Experience and Diasporan Insights for National Development,” will run from July 14–23, 2025, aligning with the National Diaspora Day and Diaspora Week celebrations in Abuja slated for July 25–26, 2025.
Bitrus added that the Convention focus on impactful engagement and collaborative action.
He recalled that Zumunta’s scholarship scheme has empowered over 5,000 science students in Northern Nigeria, with ₦100 million disbursed to date.
Bitrus added that the Association has also implemented health and palliative projects in partnership with over 30 Non-Governmental Organisations.
“We are shifting from connection to action, from diaspora dialogues to real-time delivery at home, “ he added.
Speaking in the same vein, Hon. Abike Dabiri-Erewa, Chairman/CEO Nigerians in Diaspora Commission (NIDCOM), represented by Dr. Sule Yakubu Bassi, the Secretary to the Commission, described the return of the Zumunta Convention as a milestone in diaspora engagement.
“Zumunta is demonstrating that the diaspora is not just watching, they are working. This 2025 convention showcases the power of collaboration between diaspora organisations, state governments, and federal institutions.
NIDCOM is proud to support this initiative that aligns with our mandate to promote structured, impactful diaspora contributions to national development.”

a1880.t:
CHINA-The Coordinator of the Liberian Students Union in China’s Hunan Province has highlighted various areas the Liberian Government can leverage to put the country on par with its counterparts across the globe.
Edwina Kolleh named security, education, tourism, and infrastructure development as crucial areas for possible urgent improvement.
Coordinator Kolleh said,” These sectors are not only vital to the growth of the country, but are also critical to elevating the living standards of the citizens”.
Madam Kolleh, a PhD candidate, also wants the government to pay keen attention to the promotion of the preservation of the country’s cultural values and norms, ensuring that the sector becomes a part of the governance process.
She also placed emphasis on the construction of more roads to boost trade and enhance mobility among citizens across the country.
Meanwhile, the former President of the Liberian Students in Hunan Province, Varney Johnson, is urging the Liberian government to further invest more in its Education Sector, especially in Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM).
Johnson said,” The provision of modern research equipment, coupled with the construction of conducive educational facilities across the country, will further improve Liberia’s Education Sector.
The Liberian PhD Candidate, in an ELBC interview, recently highlighted the visitation of the Academic Curriculum to include areas of research activities to broaden the minds of students in the country.
He also stressed the need for the Civil Service Agency (CSA) to be revamped, ensuring that jobs are given to citizens based on qualification, not on personal interest.
Varney Johnson noted that such a move will put Liberia on par with countries like China, the U.S, and Japan, saying that the interests of Liberians should be put at the forefront at all times.

a1896.t:
Après la région d’Ali-Sabieh, l’hôtel Gadile de la ville de Tadjourah a abrité durant deux jours, mercredi 4 et Jeudi 5 Décembre derniers, un atelier régional d’information et de sensibilisation sur le projet des filières agricoles résilientes appelé par son sigle (FAR).
Cet atelier est organisé par le Ministère de l’Agriculture, de l’Elevage et de la Pêche chargé des Ressources Halieutiques (MAEPE-RH) dans le cadre du Projet d’Appui aux Filières Agricoles Résilientes (FAR), l’Unité de Gestion du Projet (UGP). Il vise à renforcer la compétitivité et la résilience des filières agricoles, contribuant ainsi à la sécurité alimentaire et au développement économique durable. Le lancement de cet atelier, au chef-lieu de la ville blanche, a lieu en présence du préfet de la région, Mohamed Houmed Abass, Préfet de Tadjourah, du Coordinateur principal du Projet d’appui des Filières Agricoles Résilientes, Baragoïta Saïd, le sous directeur régional du Ministère de l’Agriculteur, de l’Eau, de la Pêche et de l’Elevage chargé des Ressources halieutiques, des élus locaux, des membres du club local des jeunes entrepreneurs et des nombreux agriculteurs. En premier lieu, le Préfet Mohamed Houmed Abass a exprimé son enthousiasme face à cette initiative gouvernementale. Il a affirmé sa volonté d’accompagner les acteurs du projet dans toutes les étapes de sa mise en œuvre.
Pour sa part, le coordinateur du projet en question, l’agronome Baragoïta Saïd a fait savoir aux agriculteurs régionaux de participer avec un immense plaisir cet atelier. Il a souligné la nouvelle orientation politique en matière de développement agricole, visant à améliorer la compétitivité et à répondre aux besoins du marché local.
Ces ateliers qui illustrent la volonté commune des parties prenantes de dynamiser les filières agricoles pour garantir une meilleure résilience face aux défis climatiques et économiques auront dans les chefs-lieux de toutes les régions de l’intérieur du pays. L’objectif général de ces ateliers régionaux vise à informer les populations locales, les producteurs agricoles, les investisseurs et les responsables régionaux sur le projet FAR, ses objectifs, ses composantes et les opportunités qu’il offre pour améliorer la compétitivité et la résiliente des filières agroalimentaires dans les régions de l’intérieur du pays. Quant aux objectifs spécifiques, ils consistent à sensibiliser les populations locales sur le projet FAR, ses bénéfices et les opportunités qu’il véhicule pour le développement des filières agroalimentaires des régions ciblées. Le consultant national, animateur de l’atelier à expliquer les composantes du projet, en particulier celles liées aux infrastructures de base, au soutien des agriculteurs pour accéder au financement et au développement des chaînes de valeurs agricoles.
De promouvoir la participation active des producteurs et des investisseurs agroalimentaires dans les activités du projet et la mise en œuvre des sous-projets.
De renforcer la coordination et la collaboration entre les parties prenantes locales; les autorités publiques, les institutions financières et les acteurs privés du secteur agroalimentaire.
Les résultats attendus de cet atelier appellent une meilleure compréhension des objectifs, des composantes et des mécanismes du projet FAR par les parties prenantes locales. La réussite d’une participation active des producteurs et des investisseurs dans les initiatives du projet y compris dans les sous-projets agroalimentaires. La nécessité d’une collaboration renforcée entre les autorités locales, les producteurs, les investisseurs et les partenaires techniques. L’arrêté des recommandations sur l’adaptation du projet aux besoins spécifiques des communautés locales et des producteurs dans les régions de l’intérieur du pays. La mise en œuvre du projet en question découle du constat que l’économie agricole est peu développée, les zones rurales souffre d’une pauvreté et l’importation de la quasi-totalité de la consommation alimentaire par le pays.
Au cours des dernières décennies, la politique du développement de Djibouti a été axée essentiellement sur les services en milieu urbain au détriment des zones rurales. Les agriculteurs et les éleveurs avaient bénéficié des subventions à petite échelle pour une agriculture de subsistance sans perspective de pérennité.
En raison du taux de pauvreté plus élevé en zone rurale que dans les zones urbaines, d’une production agricole faible malgré le potentiel et les importations alimentaires considérables.
A ces effets, le gouvernement a décidé de changer de paradigme de développement en mettant plus d’accent sur les investissements du secteur privé.
L’état est résolu de faciliter et d’encourager aux investisseurs privés pour un développement durable, résilient et inclusif en faveur des filières agricoles organisées et productives. Le consultant national, animateur de l’atelier a exposé aux participants les tenants et aboutissants du changement de paradigme pour le développement des zones rurales du pays. Le nouveau paradigme suit une double voie qui consiste en premier lieu à promouvoir l’entreprenariat et les investissements bancables du secteur privé en liaison avec des partenaires financiers pour une agriculture commerciale et profitable. Deuxièmement, il s’agit d’appuyer les pôles régionaux ayant un potentiel de développement où se concentreront les services et infrastructures de base.
Les buts principaux visés doivent permettre l’accroissement de la production agroalimentaire, la réduction du déficit alimentaire du pays, la création des emplois en zone rurale notamment pour les jeunes et les femmes.
Les contraintes de ce projet ambitieux à mettre en œuvre dans l’optique d’accroitre significativement sont l’impact du changement climatique, le faible niveau d’organisation du secteur agricole, l’insuffisance des infrastructures et l’enclavement des zones de production et le financement très faible du secteur au sens large du terme.
Le projet d’appui aux filières agricoles résilientes de Djibouti bénéficie d’un financement de la banque mondiale à hauteur de 17,8 millions de Dollars.
Il permettra de satisfaire les besoins économiques, l’amélioration de la sécurité alimentaire et l’innovation technologique et technique d’agriculture climato-intelligent. A et effet, les agriculteurs bénéficieront des multiples formations.
Ali Ladieh
a1896.en:
After the Ali-Sabieh region, the Gadile hotel in the town of Tadjourah hosted for two days, Wednesday 4 and Thursday 5 December, a regional information and awareness workshop on the resilient agricultural value chains project, known by its acronym (FAR).
This workshop is organised by the Ministry of Agriculture, Livestock and Fisheries in charge of Fishery Resources (MAEPE-RH) within the framework of the Support Project for Resilient Agricultural Value Chains (FAR), by the Project Management Unit (UGP). It aims to strengthen the competitiveness and resilience of agricultural value chains, thus contributing to food security and sustainable economic development. The launch of this workshop, in the capital of the white city, took place in the presence of the region's prefect, Mohamed Houmed Abass, Prefect of Tadjourah; the chief Coordinator of the Support Project for Resilient Agricultural Value Chains, Baragoïta Saïd; the regional deputy director of the Ministry of Agriculture, Water, Fisheries and Livestock in charge of Fishery Resources; local elected officials; members of the local club of young entrepreneurs; and numerous farmers. First of all, Prefect Mohamed Houmed Abass expressed his enthusiasm for this government initiative. He affirmed his willingness to support the project's actors at every stage of its implementation.
For his part, the coordinator of the project in question, the agronomist Baragoïta Saïd, informed the region's farmers that he was taking part in this workshop with immense pleasure. He underlined the new policy direction in agricultural development, aimed at improving competitiveness and responding to the needs of the local market.
These workshops, which illustrate the common will of the stakeholders to boost agricultural value chains in order to guarantee better resilience in the face of climatic and economic challenges, will be held in the capitals of all the regions of the country's interior. The general objective of these regional workshops is to inform local populations, agricultural producers, investors and regional officials about the FAR project, its objectives, its components and the opportunities it offers to improve the competitiveness and resilience of agri-food value chains in the regions of the country's interior. As for the specific objectives, they consist of raising awareness among local populations about the FAR project, its benefits and the opportunities it carries for the development of agri-food value chains in the targeted regions. The national consultant, facilitator of the workshop, explained the components of the project, in particular those linked to basic infrastructure, support for farmers in accessing financing, and the development of agricultural value chains.
To promote the active participation of agri-food producers and investors in the project's activities and the implementation of sub-projects.
To strengthen coordination and collaboration between local stakeholders: public authorities, financial institutions and private actors in the agri-food sector.
The expected results of this workshop call for a better understanding of the objectives, components and mechanisms of the FAR project by local stakeholders; the success of active participation by producers and investors in the project's initiatives, including in agri-food sub-projects; the need for strengthened collaboration between local authorities, producers, investors and technical partners; and the finalisation of recommendations on adapting the project to the specific needs of local communities and producers in the regions of the country's interior. The implementation of the project in question stems from the observation that the agricultural economy is little developed, that rural areas suffer from poverty, and that the country imports almost all of its food consumption.
In recent decades, Djibouti's development policy has focused essentially on services in urban areas to the detriment of rural areas. Farmers and livestock keepers had benefited from small-scale subsidies for subsistence agriculture without any prospect of sustainability.
This is because of the higher poverty rate in rural areas than in urban areas, weak agricultural production despite the potential, and considerable food imports.
To these ends, the government decided to change its development paradigm by placing more emphasis on private sector investments.
The state is determined to facilitate and encourage private investors towards sustainable, resilient and inclusive development in favour of organised and productive agricultural value chains. The national consultant, facilitator of the workshop, set out to participants the ins and outs of the paradigm shift for the development of the country's rural areas. The new paradigm follows a twin track which consists firstly of promoting entrepreneurship and bankable private sector investments in connection with financial partners for commercial and profitable agriculture. Secondly, it involves supporting regional hubs with development potential where basic services and infrastructure will be concentrated.
The main goals targeted must make possible the increase of agri-food production, the reduction of the country's food deficit, and the creation of jobs in rural areas, notably for young people and women.
The constraints on this ambitious project to be implemented with a view to significantly increasing production are the impact of climate change, the low level of organisation of the agricultural sector, insufficient infrastructure and the landlocked nature of production zones, and very weak financing of the sector in the broad sense of the term.
Djibouti's support project for resilient agricultural value chains benefits from World Bank financing of 17.8 million dollars.
It will make it possible to meet economic needs, improve food security, and bring technological and technical innovation in climate-smart agriculture. To this end, farmers will benefit from multiple training courses.
Ali Ladieh

a2108.t:
…Providing significant relief for developing countries
Seithati Motšoeneng
In a bold strategic move to empower low-income countries in overcoming the economic fallout from the COVID-19 pandemic and climate change, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has decisively announced a 36 percent reduction in borrowing costs.
This significant decrease which took effect on November 1 2024, translates into annual savings of $1.2 billion for developing nations, enhancing their financial capacity to “effectively tackle pressing economic challenges”.
IMF Managing Director, Kristalina Georgieva, stated at a press conference last week that the landmark decision had received unanimous backing from member states at their annual meeting in Washington, D.C.
“For the first time ever, we have lowered borrowing charges for lenders, resulting in annual savings of $1.2 billion,” she said.
Georgieva explained that the pivotal decision was rooted in a comprehensive three-pillar approach designed to drive economic growth, mobilize domestic revenues, and secure adequate financing through international financial institutions, while facilitating private sector investments at reduced costs.
This reform is set to dramatically reshape the global economic landscape by promoting productive growth and effectively addressing the challenges associated with high debt levels and low economic growth.
In a similar press conference, IMF Chairperson, Mahomed Aljadaan, asserted that these reforms were specifically crafted to ensure that low-income countries transitioned from a trajectory of low growth and high debt.
He stated: “We are committed to fostering self-lending while refining our strategies to mitigate high debt situations among low-income nations.”
Mr Aljadaan highlighted the IMF’s determined efforts to enhance capacity development assistance and secure necessary financing for these countries.
He also underscored the urgent need to improve the common framework for sovereign debt relief for lower-income nations.
This commitment is designed not only to adjust the financial terms of lending but also to safeguard the economic stability of borrowing countries while ensuring their fiscal sustainability.
However, local economists have warned that Lesotho should not be ecstatic with the IMF lifeline as the country “does not stand to benefit much.
“There won’t be too much impact to the likes of Lesotho, taking into account the debts that we already have which, are significantly high,” said independent economic analyst Thabo Qhesi.
“So, getting new loans somehow has been discouraged. Even if it does happen, it won’t be significant, it will be very minimal.”
Meanwhile, on October 21 this year, the Executive Board of the IMF announced that it had on October 11, concluded the Review of Charges and the Surcharge Policy, which for the first time jointly covered charges, surcharges, and commitment fees.
The review, the IMF noted, was part of a continuous effort to ensure the IMF’s lending policies remain fit for purpose and that the IMF could support its members in a challenging global environment.
The Executive Board further noted that it had reached a consensus on a comprehensive package of measures to “meaningfully reduce the cost of borrowing for members”, preserve incentive mechanisms for prudent and temporary borrowing, and safeguard the strength of the IMF’s balance sheet.
The reform package which is expected to lower borrowing costs by about US$1.2 billion (SDR 880 million) annually, will reduce payments on the margin of the rate of charge as well as surcharges on average by 36 percent. The number of surcharge payers is expected to decline from 20 to 13 countries (in FY2026).
“Charges and surcharges are important elements of the IMF’s cooperative lending and risk management framework. They provide incentives for prudent and temporary borrowing that help underpin the revolving nature of IMF resources and allow for the accumulation of reserves to mitigate financial risks. This supports the IMF’s financial foundation, enabling it to play its role as a lender at the center of the global financial safety net,” the IMF Executive Board said.
The IMF Executive Board approved the following changes:
i) Lowering the margin paid over the SDR interest rate by 40 percent, to 60 basis points from 100 basis points.
ii) Increasing the borrowing threshold above which surcharges apply by 60 percent, to 300 percent of quota from 187.5 percent of quota.
iii) Aligning the thresholds above which commitment fees apply to the overall annual and cumulative access limits under the GRA (200 and 600 percent of quota, respectively); and
iv) Reducing the time-based surcharge rate by 25 percent, to 75 basis points from 100 basis points.
v) Setting a regular review cycle for the surcharge policy to allow for timely assessments and updates to the surcharge policy framework, every five years or earlier if warranted.
vi) Strengthening disclosures and operational procedures to ensure that the authorities have adequate information on the cost of Fund borrowing earlier in negotiations of GRA financing.

a2130.t:
"Penso, como sabem, que a resposta em Gaza, na Faixa de Gaza, tem sido excessiva", considerou Joe Biden, numa troca de palavras com jornalistas na Casa Branca, na quinta-feira.
O exército israelita intensificou, na quinta-feira, os ataques a Rafah, no sul da Faixa de Gaza, e Washington alertou Telavive, aliada histórica dos EUA, para o risco de uma catástrofe nesta cidade.
"Estou a insistir muito, muito mesmo, para que a ajuda humanitária chegue a Gaza", disse Biden.
A ofensiva de Israel causou até ao momento mais de 27.800 mortos e 61.317 feridos na Faixa de Gaza, de acordo com dados do ministério da Saúde local controlado pelo Hamas.
No ataque do movimento islamita palestiniano Hamas a Israel em 07 de Outubro, que originou a resposta israelita, foram mortas 1.140 pessoas, na maioria civis mas também perto de 400 militares, de acordo com os últimos números oficiais israelitas.
a2130.en:
"I think, as you know, that the response in Gaza, in the Gaza Strip, has been excessive," Joe Biden said in an exchange with journalists at the White House on Thursday.
The Israeli army stepped up attacks on Rafah, in the south of the Gaza Strip, on Thursday, and Washington warned Tel Aviv, a historic US ally, of the risk of a catastrophe in that city.
"I am pushing very, very hard for humanitarian aid to reach Gaza," Biden said.
Israel's offensive has so far caused more than 27,800 deaths and 61,317 injuries in the Gaza Strip, according to data from the local Health Ministry controlled by Hamas.
In the attack by the Palestinian Islamist movement Hamas on Israel on 7 October, which triggered the Israeli response, 1,140 people were killed, mostly civilians but also nearly 400 military personnel, according to the latest official Israeli figures.

a2229.t:
En raison des troubles post-électoraux es milliers de réfugiés et de civils mozambicains sont confrontés à d’immenses risques, perdent leurs moyens de subsistance et dépendent de l’aide humanitaire, alerte le HCR.
Au Mozambique, les troubles post-électoraux ont forcé des milliers de personnes à fuir leur foyer. Au Malawi, le HCR, l’agence des Nations Unies pour les réfugiés, et le gouvernement ont identifié environ 2 000 personnes qui ont traversé la frontière la semaine dernière. Dans l’Eswatini voisin, 1 000 autres personnes sont arrivées, poursuit l’organisme onusien.
Parmi les nouveaux arrivants figurent des réfugiés et des demandeurs d’asile de diverses nationalités qui vivaient au Mozambique, précise le HCR qui dit s’inquiéter de l’escalade des déplacements et de son impact sur les populations touchées.
« Nous sommes profondément alarmés par la situation actuelle au Mozambique, où l’escalade de la violence a forcé des milliers de personnes à fuir. Les réfugiés et les civils sont confrontés à d’immenses risques, perdent leurs moyens de subsistance et dépendent de l’aide humanitaire. Bien que nous soyons reconnaissants de la générosité du Malawi et de l’Eswatini, un soutien immédiat est crucial pour faire face à l’aggravation de la crise et prévenir de nouvelles souffrances », a déclaré Chansa Kapaya, directrice régionale du HCR pour l’Afrique australe.
Au Malawi, les personnes qui ont fui le Mozambique ont déclaré avoir échappé aux attaques et aux pillages dans leurs villages. Beaucoup ont parcouru de longues distances et ont traversé la rivière Shire à pied ou en petites embarcations pour se mettre en sécurité. Parmi elles se trouvent des femmes enceintes, des personnes âgées et des enfants qui ont eu peu à manger, affirme le HCR.
Ce dernier soutient avoir rapidement fourni des tentes, des couvertures et des kits d’hygiène pour aider les plus vulnérables, mais d’importantes lacunes subsistent en matière d’aide humanitaire.
« Les abris sont surpeuplés, les installations sanitaires sont inadéquates et l’accès à la nourriture et à l’eau potable est insuffisant. Plus de 1 000 personnes partagent une seule latrine sur certains sites, ce qui augmente considérablement le risque de maladie », note-t-il.
Selon le HCR, en Eswatini, de nombreux nouveaux arrivants déclarent avoir perdu leurs commerces et entreprises en raison des violences. Le centre d’accueil des réfugiés de Malindza, initialement conçu pour 250 personnes, est désormais surpeuplé et abrite plus de 1 000 personnes.
Le HCR collabore avec les autorités locales et ses partenaires pour fournir une assistance, mais des ressources supplémentaires sont nécessaires de toute urgence pour soutenir la réponse et se préparer à accueillir davantage d’arrivées, signale l’organisation humanitaire.
Le Mozambique se remet encore des effets dévastateurs du cyclone Chido, qui a frappé les régions il y a quelques semaines. La situation actuelle entrave les efforts humanitaires essentiels pour les communautés qui ont tout perdu dans la tempête, tout en rendant plus difficile la réponse pour les aider.
La situation au Malawi et en Eswatini devient critique, le nombre croissant de réfugiés et de demandeurs d’asile mettant à rude épreuve des ressources déjà très limitées.
La communauté internationale doit d’urgence apporter un soutien aux pays d’accueil et veiller à ce que les populations touchées reçoivent l’aide dont elles ont désespérément besoin, conclut le HCR dans sa note parvenue ce mardi à APA.
ARD/ac/Sf/APA
a2229.en:
Because of post-electoral unrest, thousands of Mozambican refugees and civilians are facing immense risks, losing their livelihoods and depending on humanitarian aid, UNHCR warns.

In Mozambique, post-electoral unrest has forced thousands of people to flee their homes. In Malawi, UNHCR, the United Nations refugee agency, and the government have identified around 2,000 people who crossed the border last week. In neighbouring Eswatini, another 1,000 people have arrived, the UN body continues.

Among the new arrivals are refugees and asylum seekers of various nationalities who were living in Mozambique, specifies UNHCR, which says it is worried about the escalation of displacement and its impact on affected populations.

"We are deeply alarmed by the current situation in Mozambique, where the escalation of violence has forced thousands of people to flee. Refugees and civilians face immense risks, lose their livelihoods and depend on humanitarian aid. Although we are grateful for the generosity of Malawi and Eswatini, immediate support is crucial to deal with the worsening crisis and prevent further suffering," said Chansa Kapaya, UNHCR Regional Director for Southern Africa.

In Malawi, the people who fled Mozambique said they had escaped attacks and looting in their villages. Many travelled long distances and crossed the Shire River on foot or in small boats to reach safety. Among them are pregnant women, elderly people and children who have had little to eat, UNHCR states.

The agency maintains that it quickly provided tents, blankets and hygiene kits to help the most vulnerable, but that significant gaps remain in humanitarian aid.

"Shelters are overcrowded, sanitation facilities are inadequate and access to food and drinking water is insufficient. More than 1,000 people share a single latrine at some sites, which considerably increases the risk of disease," it notes.

According to UNHCR, in Eswatini many new arrivals report having lost their shops and businesses because of the violence. The Malindza refugee reception centre, initially designed for 250 people, is now overcrowded and houses more than 1,000 people.

UNHCR is working with local authorities and its partners to provide assistance, but additional resources are urgently needed to support the response and to prepare to receive more arrivals, the humanitarian organisation reports.

Mozambique is still recovering from the devastating effects of Cyclone Chido, which struck the regions a few weeks ago. The current situation hampers essential humanitarian efforts for communities that lost everything in the storm, while making it more difficult to respond to help them.

The situation in Malawi and Eswatini is becoming critical, with the growing number of refugees and asylum seekers putting a severe strain on already very limited resources.

The international community must urgently provide support to host countries and ensure that affected populations receive the aid they desperately need, UNHCR concludes in its note received by APA on Tuesday.

ARD/ac/Sf/APA

a2373.t:
MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has embarked on an undisclosed visit to the United Arab Emirates (UAE), as his government grapples with significant financial challenges following the United States’ decision to cut financial assistance to Mogadishu.
The visit comes at a delicate time, with Somalia accusing the UAE of undermining its sovereignty. The Gulf nation recently sparked controversy by inviting the leader of Somaliland, Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, to the World Governments Summit.
Somaliland, a breakaway region that has operated as a de facto independent state for over three decades, is still recognized by Somalia as part of its territory. Mogadishu has consistently opposed Somaliland’s efforts to gain international recognition.
Somali Foreign Minister Ahmed Moalim Fiqi recently stated that the government would take decisive action against Abu Dhabi for what it perceives as a violation of Somalia’s sovereignty. However, State Minister of Foreign Affairs Ali Bal’ad downplayed the incident, describing it as “not a big deal” and highlighting the UAE’s longstanding support for Somalia.
The UAE has been a key ally of the current Somali administration, funding the training of tens of thousands of Somali security forces and providing critical financial and logistical support. Despite the recent tensions, the UAE’s role in Somalia’s stabilization efforts remains significant.
President Mohamud’s visit to the UAE is expected to include high-level meetings with Emirati officials, though the agenda remains undisclosed. The trip underscores the complex dynamics between the two nations, balancing diplomatic tensions with strategic partnerships.
Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

a2449.t:
Les membres de la Fédération nationale des tisseuses du Burkina (FENATI-BF) ont tenu leur première assemblée générale de l’année le jeudi 20 février 2025 à Ouagadougou. L’ordre du jour portait sur le bilan des activités de l’année écoulée et les perspectives pour le rayonnement de la fédération.
La Fédération Nationale des tisseuses du Burkina (FENATI-BF) s’est fixée pour objectif de promouvoir et de valoriser le Faso Dan Fani. Elle est ainsi composée d’unions de tisseuses dans les 13 régions du pays, elles-mêmes constituées d’associations de base dans les provinces et communes. Après une année d’activité, un bilan s’imposait.
C’est dans ce contexte que Germaine Compaoré, secrétaire général de la FENATI-BF, a souligné que le programme d’activité de 2024, avait été riche en événements, avec des succès et des défis à relever.
« Dans l’exécution du programme d’activité de 2024, nous avons traversé des pluies et de beaux temps, des vents et marées, des hauts et des bas, nous avons vécu des succès et des échecs mais nous sommes arrivées à bonne destination », a-t-elle déclaré.
Parmi les acquis, la secrétaire générale a notamment cité la reconnaissance de la FENATI par le gouvernement et les institutions du Burkina Faso, la participation à des instances de décision importantes, la collaboration avec la Chambre de Métiers et de l’Artisanat du Burkina Faso (CMA-BF), le ministère en charge de l’Artisanat et des actions humanitaires. Elle a également mentionné que la FENATI et certains de ses membres ont reçu des distinctions honorifiques. Malgré les acquis, elle a déploré des défis qui persistent.
« Quant aux difficultés nous pouvons noter la faible organisation des tisseuses dans certaines régions, l’utilisation du fil importer dans certaines régions malgré la sensibilisation, le manque de fil de couleur FILSAH pour le moment, manque de formation pour la grande masse des tisseuses, la non adhésion de certaines tisseuses aux structures des tisseuses organisées, l’inondation des marchés par le fil et pagnes tissés importés, la non distinction des consommateurs entre le Faso dan Fani et le pagne tissé importé malgré la sensibilisation », a-t-elle cité.
En termes de perspectives, les membres de la FENATI ont décidé de poursuivre la sensibilisation dans les régions où le fil importé est très utilisé, afin d’encourager l’utilisation du fil burkinabé. elles ont également pour objectif de mobiliser des fonds pour une vaste campagne de formation de masse aux techniques de teinture artisanale durable et de tissage normalisé dans toutes les régions, afin d’améliorer la qualité et la quantité du Faso Dan Fani. Enfin, la FENATI souhaite acquérir un terrain et y construire son siège.
Aminata Catherine SANOU
Burkina 24
a2449.en:
The members of the National Federation of Women Weavers of Burkina (FENATI-BF) held their first general assembly of the year on Thursday 20 February 2025 in Ouagadougou. The agenda covered the review of the past year's activities and the prospects for the federation's development.

The National Federation of Women Weavers of Burkina (FENATI-BF) has set itself the objective of promoting and adding value to Faso Dan Fani. It is made up of unions of women weavers in the country's 13 regions, themselves made up of grassroots associations in the provinces and communes. After a year of activity, a review was needed.

It is in this context that Germaine Compaore, secretary general of FENATI-BF, stressed that the 2024 activity programme had been rich in events, with successes and challenges to overcome.

"In carrying out the 2024 activity programme, we went through rain and fair weather, through wind and tide, through ups and downs, we experienced successes and failures but we reached our destination," she declared.

Among the achievements, the secretary general notably cited the recognition of FENATI by the government and the institutions of Burkina Faso, participation in important decision-making bodies, collaboration with the Chamber of Trades and Crafts of Burkina Faso (CMA-BF), the ministry in charge of Crafts and humanitarian actions. She also mentioned that FENATI and some of its members had received honorary distinctions. Despite the achievements, she deplored challenges that persist.

"As for the difficulties, we can note the weak organisation of women weavers in certain regions, the use of imported thread in certain regions despite awareness-raising, the current lack of FILSAH coloured thread, the lack of training for the great mass of women weavers, the failure of certain women weavers to join organised weavers' structures, the flooding of markets with imported thread and woven wrappers, and consumers' failure to distinguish between Faso Dan Fani and imported woven wrappers despite awareness-raising," she listed.

In terms of prospects, the members of FENATI decided to continue awareness-raising in the regions where imported thread is heavily used, in order to encourage the use of Burkinabe thread. They also aim to mobilise funds for a vast mass-training campaign in sustainable artisanal dyeing techniques and standardised weaving in all regions, in order to improve the quality and quantity of Faso Dan Fani. Finally, FENATI wishes to acquire land and build its headquarters there.

Aminata Catherine SANOU
Burkina 24

a2547.t:
Approximately 300 migrants attempting to cross the central Mediterranean were intercepted and returned to the Libyan coast between May 25 and May 31, 2025, according to a report by the International Organization for Migration (IOM).
This latest wave of interceptions underscores the ongoing migration crisis along the perilous maritime route from North Africa to Europe.
The operations took place off the shores of several key Libyan coastal towns, including Zuwara, Sabratha, Azzawiya, Tripoli, and Al-Khums, all recognized as primary departure points for migrant boats.
Since the beginning of 2025, the IOM has documented the return of 9,585 migrants to Libya. This figure includes 8,147 men, 960 women, and 333 children, with 145 identified as unaccompanied minors or individuals requiring special assistance. As of May 31, 2025, the human cost of these journeys remains high, with at least 233 migrants having lost their lives at sea and another 225 reported missing.
Despite the extreme dangers and widespread criticism regarding reception conditions in Libya, attempts to cross the Mediterranean continue. In 2024, 21,762 migrants were intercepted and returned, with 665 deaths and 1,034 missing. The preceding year saw 962 deaths and 1,536 missing at sea.
The IOM consistently reiterates its stance that Libya cannot be considered a safe port for the disembarkation of migrants. While the organization is not involved in the interception operations themselves, it provides vital humanitarian assistance upon the migrants’ return, simultaneously advocating for sustainable alternatives that uphold fundamental human rights.
SL/te/Sf/fss/abj/APA

a2551.t:
The United States, through the US Agency for International Development (USAID) has donated a $220,000 mobile health clinic van to HopeXchange Medical Center in Kumasi to facilitate medical outreach for Ghanaians.
Dr. Zohra Balsara, Health Office Director USAID, Ghana at the handing over ceremony explained that the mobile clinic is equipped with an ultrasound machine and printer, an echocardiogram machine, two examination beds, three consulting rooms, air conditioners, a refrigerator for Vaccines, a generator and power system.
According to her, HopeXchange Medical Center in Kumasi will manage and operate the clinic and provide specialized medical screenings to communities in the Ashanti region and beyond.
She expressed the hope that with the introduction of the mobile clinic, preventive, promotive and curative health services would be brought to the doorsteps of those who are unable to travel to Kumasi.
Dr. Zohra, USAID/Ghana Health Office Director said the beauty of the HopeXchange model is that everyone has the right to the highest level of quality health care, embodying a true vision of equity.
She said the HopeXchange Medical Center is a state-of-the-art health care facility managed by the Christian Health Authority of Ghana (CHAG) that serves four million people across Ghana.
According to her, USAID has since 2013 provided $3.5 million to HopeXchange to, among other things, establish and equip its pathology laboratory for the women’s Cancer Center, support clinical and research programmes, and construct a maternal-child health center with a labor and delivery suite, neonatal and pediatric intensive care unitsand an adolescent clinic.
Mr. Dominic Osei Kofi, General Manager of HopeXchange receiving the Mobile Clinic Van expressed gratitude to the partnership of USAID/ASHA.
He said the HopeXchange Medical Center has a dedicated outreach team of clinicians that conduct routine outreach to communities, and that last year October 2023 to September 2024, the outreach team researched 12,517 people across 63 communities in the Ashanti and Bono East regions.
Mr. Osei Kofi expressed optimism that the Mobile Clinic Van would enable the outreach team to significantly expand its Community services and augment their outreach activities.
He revealed that Medical screening in rural and poor Communities has been part of their services even before the start of the hospital and now one of their core activities.
He said their robust and dedicated Outreach Team of clinicians reach out to communities within the Ashanti and Bono East regions with health education and medical screening at no cost to the people.
General Manager Osei Kofi indicated that about 20 persons identified with masses in their breasts during various outreaches received various interventions ranging from ultrasound and ICT scans, histopathological diagnosis to free surgery and that they returned home with renewed hope for life.
The General Manager re-affirmed that the Mobile Clinic would allow the Outreach Team to reach underserved and remote Communities nationwide, offering health education and medical screenings including specialized services.He said it will also provide essential free quality medical care to people who otherwise lack access, including children in need.

a2764.t:
U.S. Marine Corps General Michael Langley, commander of U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM), visited Maputo, Mozambique August 15-16 during an official trip to partner countries in southern Africa. This visit reinforces the U.S. government’s partnership with Mozambique to build a peaceful and prosperous future. General Langley travelled to Mozambique together with Deputy for Civil-Military Engagement Ambassador Robert Scott, and USAID Senior Developmental Advisor Maura Barry Boyle, emphasizing the importance of an integrated partnership across defence, diplomacy, and development.
In Maputo, General Langley met with President Filipe Nyusi and with the Chief of General Staff Admiral Joaquim Mangrasse. The officials discussed the importance of the U.S.-Mozambique security partnership and progress in stabilizing the situation in northern Mozambique. General Langley engaged non-governmental and civil society leaders on the challenges facing Mozambique and the opportunities for coordination on both government- and community-led efforts to end the conflict in Cabo Delgado and accelerate development.
“Mozambique is a strategic partner of the United States,” said Ambassador Vrooman. “Our two countries continue to work together to strengthen ties in a wide range of areas, including issues related to security, but also development, investment, and infrastructure.”
“I came here to discuss with Mozambique’s security leaders how we find opportunities to address our shared challenges together,” said General Langley. “We discussed how we can achieve our common goals and expand our partnership. This includes integrating defence with diplomacy and development – the three Ds – to support our partners in Mozambique and build resilience to conflict and the myriad of challenges facing Mozambicans on a daily basis.”
“We want the people of Mozambique to know, we are committed to our partnership and visits like today further expand the dialogue which inevitably produce dividends,” added Deputy Commander Ambassador Scott. Senior Advisor Boyle said, “We also recognize the important work of those dedicated to addressing the challenges associated with marginalized groups.”
General Langley became the 6th commander of United States Africa Command in August 2022. Headquartered in Stuttgart, Germany, U.S. AFRICOM is one of six joint service geographic combatant commands and is responsible for all U.S. military operations and activities to protect and advance U.S. national interests in Africa.
The AFRICOM Commander’s visit comes after U.S. Secretary of Defence Lloyd J. Austin III met with President Nyusi in Washington at the 2022 U.S.-African Leaders Summit, and after the two leaders spoke via phone on August 2. In July, U.S. Assistant Secretary of Defence for Special Operations and Low Intensity Conflict Chris Maier and AFRICOM’s Director of Military Intelligence Brigadier General Rose Keravuori visited Maputo. In addition to increased engagement between senior officials, the U.S.-Mozambique security partnership has also expanded in the realm of training. Since 2021, the U.S. Department of Defence conducted five Joint Combined Exchange Training (JCET) programs between U.S. Special Operations Forces and Mozambican Commandos and Fuzileiros. The U.S. Department of Defence also conducted numerous tactical combat casualty care (TCCC) and combat lifesaver training courses for the armed forces. Mozambican forces recently participated in a second multinational maritime exercise Cutlass Express and continues its long-standing participation in the International Military Education and Training (IMET) program.
In April 2022, the U.S. government selected Mozambique as a priority country for the U.S. Strategy to Prevent Conflict and Promote Stability. With partners, the United States is coordinating its development, diplomatic, and security-sector assistance through a ten-year plan to prevent violence, promote stability, and build resilience in Cabo Delgado and neighbouring provinces.
